2. Which of the following PBF findings is least likely to be seen in patients with iron deficiency anemia?

3. An 8-year-old boy is brought with blood in the urine. His mother says he had bloody diarrhea, fever, and vomiting 10 days ago. His BP is 130/90 mm Hg, and he is jaundiced. Investigations reveal a platelet count of 50,000 cells/cu mm, BUN of 35 mg/dl, and creatinine of 3.5 mg/dl. Which of the following cells would you expect to see in the peripheral smear?
4. A patient has a HbA2 of 3% and HbF of 97%. A peripheral blood smear is taken. Which of the following blood pictures will be seen in this patient?

5. A child presents with anemia, frontal bossing and jaundice. Which of the following statements are true for the given condition?
1. Ineffective erythropoiesis
2. Systemic iron overload
3. Intravascular hemolysis
4. Increased hepcidin degradation
6. You are examining the peripheral smear of a patient with anaemia and see the following finding. Name the finding and its pathogenesis.
options: Howell Jolly body - ineffective RBC enucleation
